segments: ... against Jawali, he alone,
and struck the hand of the standard-bearer and severed it,
and struck Jawali himself with the sword,
but the chain mail which he wore protected him from harm.
Then the men of Jawali and Ridwan's side, when they saw that Qilij Arslan alone was displaying strength,
took courage against those of his side,
and routed and put them to flight.
When Qilij Arslan saw that the men of his army had fled,
and had left him alone,
he feared for his life,
thinking that even if these men did not kill him,
yet when he was bound and taken to the Sultan,
he would never leave him alive,
because he had abolished the proclamation of his name from Mosul.
Therefore he threw himself, while mounted, into the river Khabur,
while shooting arrows from within the water at those who pursued after him.
And because the iron coat of mail which was on him and on his horse was heavy,
and also on account of his shooting {with a cross-bow?}, the horse stumbled in a deep place,
and both he and the horse drowned.
And after some days he was cast out from the water onto the river bank,
and was taken and buried in a village called Damsham
(Damsham).
And while Ridwan went toward Callinicus (Raqqa),
Jawali came to Mosul.
And the market-folk who were in it quickly opened the gates to him,
and he entered the city.
And he seized a certain eunuch from among the slaves of Jakarmish,
and took from him forty thousand gold dinars.
And he sent word to Bazmish
to surrender the citadel,
and return everything that he had taken from Mosul,
and go in peace to his country with what he had brought with him.
Bazmish, however, was not able to resist,
because hope was cut off from him by the death of Qilij Arslan his master.
Rather, he quickly came down,
and took the wife of Qilij Arslan and all their people,
and they went to Melitene,
except Malik-Shah, the son of Qilij Arslan {OCR: Nalij Arslan},
because Jawali sent him to the Sultan.
And he went to Jazirat [Ibn Umar],
and besieged it.
And when Habashi, the son of Jakarmish, gave him six thousand dinars and an Arab horse,
he left it and returned to Mosul.
And he dismissed Ibn Shahrazuri from the judgeship,
and appointed in it Abu Bakr of Erbil.
And when a victory like this had occurred for Jawali,
he was puffed up in his spirit,
